activity_context.topic_title: The First Shifting Theorem of Laplace Transforms

feedback.problem: Given that  $L{t\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}}{({s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2})^{2}},$ find the Laplace transform $L{{e}^{4t}\cdot t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The first shifting theorem states that if
$L{f(t)}=F(s),$
then
$L{{e}^{at}f(t)}=F(s-a).$

Using the given result, we have

$$
L{t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)}=\frac{{s}^{2}-{3}^{2}}{({s}^{2}+{3}^{2})^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, applying the first shifting theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{4t}\cdot t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)} & =\frac{(s-4)^{2}-{3}^{2}}{((s-4)^{2}+{3}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(s-4)^{2}-9}{((s-4)^{2}+9)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
